open_prs.title: fix(init): end tracees with kill(2) instead of PTRACE_KILL
open_prs.body:
Fixes #225

## Summary

- `native_fail` and the domain-stop paths of `native` and Gate 1 ended their tracee with `PTRACE_KILL` and then reaped it. When a seccomp policy refuses `PTRACE_KILL`, the reap blocked with the tracee in its stop; on the `native` and `process-native` setup failures, before `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL` is set, the tracee ran on untraced once the blocked supervisor was killed (#225).
- A new `kill_tracee` sends `SIGKILL` with `kill(2)` and reaps, as `launch_fail` does. `native_fail`, both domain-stop paths and `supervise_setup_fail` (Gate 1 setup) use it. `PTRACE_KILL` remains only as a fallback when `kill(2)` fails: the native tracee runs as UID 1000, so a supervisor without `CAP_KILL` can only end it through the tracer relationship.
- Some `native_fail` callers have already reaped the child (`did not stop after exec`, `escaped supervision`), where the old `PTRACE_KILL` just returned `ESRCH`. `kill_tracee` first does a nonblocking `wait4` on the pid and returns if the child is gone (`ECHILD`) or has just been reaped, so `kill(2)` only reaches a child that is still ours and whose pid cannot have been reused.
- `process_native_fail` no longer sends anything to the root task. Every caller runs after `PTRACE_SETOPTIONS` set `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`, which fork, vfork and clone children inherit, so the exit in `domain_fail` kills every tracee; the root may already be reaped at some callers, and reaping it there could block on traced threads.
- Output and exit status are unchanged on every path.

## Changes

- `crates/ginux-init/src/main.rs`: `kill_tracee`, used by `native_fail`, the `native` and Gate 1 domain-stop paths and `supervise_setup_fail`; `process_native_fail` relies on `PTRACE_O_EXITKILL`.
- `tests/fixtures/gate1-setup-fixture.c`: `deny-ptrace <request> <program> [args...]` passes the remaining arguments on (it passed only the program before; `test-gate1-setup.py` is unaffected).
- `scripts/test-tracee-kill.py`: five checks in a private mount namespace with a temporary directory bound over `/var/tmp`: `native` and `process-native` with every request but `PTRACE_TRACEME` refused (exit 1, failure reason, payload never runs); `native` and Gate 1 with only `PTRACE_KILL` refused (exit 0, `GINUX_NATIVE_CHECK: PASS` / `GATE1: PASS`); `native` with `CAP_KILL` dropped from the bounding set (`setpriv`), which covers the fallback.
- `Makefile` (`test-tracee-kill`), `.github/workflows/check.yml` (`sudo make test-tracee-kill` in `launch-integration`), `README.md` (Linux integration steps), `docs/gate-1-foundation.md` (one sentence after the setup-failure paragraph).

## Testing

`scripts/test-tracee-kill.py` with `main`'s binary (3f2fe7df) fails its first four checks in 10 of 10 runs (output in #225); the `CAP_KILL` check passes there, since `main` uses `PTRACE_KILL`. A variant of this change without the `PTRACE_KILL` fallback hangs in the `CAP_KILL` check (`exit=timeout`). With this change all five checks pass in 10 of 10 runs, and `test-gate1-setup` passes in 10 of 10 runs.

| scenario | `main` | this change |
|---|---|---|
| `native`, every request but `PTRACE_TRACEME` refused | hangs in `wait4`; after the supervisor is killed the payload runs | `GINUX_DOMAIN: failed reason=native ptrace setup failed`, exit 1, payload never runs |
| `process-native`, same | hangs; payload runs afterwards | `GINUX_DOMAIN: failed reason=process ptrace options failed`, exit 1, payload never runs |
| `native`, only `PTRACE_KILL` refused | hangs after `emulate result=domain-stop` | `GINUX_NATIVE_CHECK: PASS`, exit 0 |
| Gate 1 with `managed-payload`, only `PTRACE_KILL` refused | hangs at the payload's `exit` | `GATE1: PASS`, exit 0 |
| `native` without `CAP_KILL` | `GINUX_NATIVE_CHECK: PASS` | `GINUX_NATIVE_CHECK: PASS` (fallback) |

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check`, `make check` (incl. clippy), `make test-unit`, `make build`, `make test-process-native` | pass |
| `make test-launch`, `make test-native-supervision`, `make test-gate1-setup` and `make test-tracee-kill` as root on x86-64 Linux | pass |
| `make host-boot-test` and `make test` (Rocky host VM suite, QEMU TCG, macOS arm64) | pass |

open_prs.title: fix(process): skip clone tid stores the caller cannot write like Linux
open_prs.body:
Fixes #223

## Summary

- `clone` published the virtual tid into the `CLONE_PARENT_SETTID` and `CLONE_CHILD_SETTID` cells with `PTRACE_POKETEXT`. A ptrace write ignores page protections, so a cell in read-only memory was written. An unmapped cell made the store fail, and the supervisor failed the domain. Linux stores both cells with `put_user` and ignores a fault (`kernel_clone` for the parent cell, `schedule_tail` in the child for the child cell): `clone` succeeds and the memory stays untouched.
- `store_tracee_tid` now uses the all-or-nothing 4-byte store that #221 added for the wait4 status, renamed from `store_tracee_status` to `store_tracee_u32`. It writes through `write_tracee_bytes` and so honors the tracee's page protections. A cell that crosses a page boundary is written all or nothing, like the kernel's single store.
- `-EFAULT` from that store is ignored, at all three call sites: the parent cell of a process clone, the parent cell of a thread or another `CLONE_VM` clone (such as `CLONE_VM | CLONE_VFORK`), and the child cell at the child's first stop. A skipped store is recorded with a new audit line `tid store fault virtual-tid=N`; the thread site then no longer claims `thread-tid virtual-tid=N`. Any other error (for example `ESRCH` for a tracee that is gone) keeps the existing killed-task check and domain failure.
- On the ptrace fallback of `write_tracee_bytes` (no `process_vm_writev`), an unmapped cell is now skipped as well. A read-only cell is still written there, as before this change.

Details and reproduction: #223.

## Changes

- `crates/ginux-init/src/main.rs`: `store_tracee_tid` calls `store_tracee_u32`, audits and skips `-EFAULT`, and returns whether the tid was stored; the thread site prints `thread-tid virtual-tid=N` only then. `store_tracee_status` becomes `store_tracee_u32` (same code, generic parameter names). The now unused `poke_tracee_bytes` import is dropped.
- `tests/fixtures/process-review-fixture.c`: scenarios `ro_clone_tid`, `bad_clone_tid` and `straddle_clone_tid`. Each one creates a process with both tid flags (no `CLONE_VM`, so the child cell is in the child's own copy), waits for it, then creates a thread with both tid flags, all with the tid pointers at a read-only cell, an unmapped address, or a cell crossing into an unmapped page. The parent, the child and the thread print the clone result, the read-only word and the bytes before the end of the bss page.
- `scripts/test-process-native.py`: expected lines for these scenarios, the same as natively, with 20 repetitions each, and a check that all four tid stores (parent and child cell, process and thread) were audited as skipped and no `thread-tid` publication was claimed. `ro_clone_tid` and `bad_clone_tid` also get the `/vm-writev-enosys` and `/vm-writev-eperm` modes. There `bad_clone_tid` expects the same lines, and `ro_clone_tid` expects the reduced-fidelity result (the tid written into the read-only cell, no skipped store), which a plain mode also accepts where the supervisor reports the fallback. `straddle_clone_tid` has no fallback mode, like `straddle_status`: the page after its cell is unmapped, so the store faults at the `PTRACE_PEEKTEXT` of that page before any write.
- `Makefile`: the three scenarios added to `build-process-fixtures`.

## Testing

The three scenarios fail on `main`'s binary (3f2fe7df): `ro_clone_tid` with the virtual tid in the read-only cell (`process ro cell=2`, `child ro cell=2`, `thread ro cell=3`), `bad_clone_tid` and `straddle_clone_tid` with `GINUX_DOMAIN: failed reason=child tid store failed` (or `clone parent tid store failed`). With this change all three pass 20 of 20 runs in each of two full runs, and so do the four new `/vm-writev-*` modes.

| case | Linux (pid namespace) | `main` | this change |
|---|---|---|---|
| tid cells in `.rodata`, process and thread (`ro_clone_tid`) | created, cell `0` | created, cell `2` (process, both sides) and `3` (thread) | created, cell `0` |
| tid cells unmapped (`bad_clone_tid`) | created | domain failure | created |
| tid cells crossing into an unmapped page (`straddle_clone_tid`) | created, both bytes untouched | domain failure | created, both bytes untouched |
| each flag alone, process and thread (manual probes, unmapped and crossing cell) | created | domain failure (`clone parent tid`, `thread tid` or `child tid store failed`) | created |
| each flag alone, process and thread (manual probes, read-only cell) | created, cell `0` | created, the side that stores sees `2` or `3` | created, cell `0` |
| `ro_clone_tid` with `process_vm_writev` unavailable (fallback) | as above | cell `2`/`3` | cell `2`/`3` (reduced fidelity, as `main`) |
| `bad_clone_tid` with `process_vm_writev` unavailable (fallback) | as above | domain failure | created |
| `straddle_clone_tid` with `process_vm_writev` failing for the whole run (`ENOSYS` and `EPERM` wraps below) | as above | domain failure | created, both bytes untouched |
| valid tid cells (`clone_tid`, `unused_parent_tid`) | virtual tid stored in both cells | pass | pass |

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check`, `make check` (incl. clippy), `make test-unit`, `make build` | pass |
| `make test-process-native` (all scenarios incl. the three new ones, the twelve `/vm-writev-*` modes and `legacy`), twice | pass |
| `make test-process-native` with `process_vm_writev` failing for the whole run, once with `ENOSYS`, once with `EPERM` | pass |
| `make test` (Rocky host VM suite, QEMU TCG, macOS arm64) | pass |

open_prs.title: feat(console): support bounded polling of standard descriptors
open_prs.body:
Programs using `poll` to wait for standard input or output readiness currently receive a policy denial in native execution. This adds a bounded allowance for descriptors 0–2 (plus ignored negative entries), with at most 16 entries and a timeout of 0–300 seconds. The supervisor validates the descriptor array before continuation; other descriptors, unreadable arrays, and unbounded waits remain denied.

Based directly on `main` at `0e06a986`. The launch fixture covers readiness, timeout limits, invalid pointers, descriptor restrictions, and closed descriptors.

Validation passed: `make check`, `make test-unit` (54 tests), release build, `test-launch`, `test-native-supervision`, and `test-process-native`.

163.author: gmkurtzer
163.body: Confirmed from the current balanced argument check: syscall 318 compares arg2, which is flags, so the intended 256-byte buflen bound is ineffective. This is a current userspace-kernel policy decision, so I am leaving the issue open. My recommendation is option 2: clamp rsi to 256 before mediation and expose the kernel-permitted short read. That preserves the intended per-call resource bound without turning larger glibc arc4random_buf requests into fatal errors. Maintainer approval is needed before implementation because this intentionally changes observable syscall behavior; no implementation work has been authorized or started.

178.author: gmkurtzer
178.body:
Maintainer review: the core claim is confirmed on current `main`. `balanced_arguments_allowed` rejects `read`/`pread64` above 1 MiB and `write` above 4096 bytes, and the launch path turns that policy failure into EPERM rather than a legal short transfer.

This should follow the same policy decision as #163. My recommended implementation is to clamp the length register before mediation so callers observe ordinary short-transfer semantics, with focused launch regressions for each syscall. Keep `writev` out of that first change unless its aggregate-byte accounting can be made independently reviewable; its iovec-count limit is a related but distinct contract.

Please hold the PR until Gregory confirms that shared clamping direction, because it changes observable syscall behavior. No further reproduction evidence is needed.

179.author: gmkurtzer
179.body:
Maintainer review: the policy-surface claim is confirmed on current `main`; the listed syscall numbers are absent from `balanced_surface` and therefore fall through to ENOSYS. This is relevant to the maintained userspace shim, but it is a bundle of policy decisions rather than one mechanical fix.

Please hold implementation while we choose the contract. My recommended split is: (1) process-local compatibility such as getcwd, dup/dup2/dup3, chdir/fchdir, sleep, and read-only xattr calls; (2) virtualized identity/state such as uname, umask, times, and selected scheduler/group queries; and (3) separate isolation work for `/proc` identity and audit/workload stderr framing. Host-identity or host-topology leakage should not be admitted merely for compatibility.

Focused PRs with one coherent policy group and launch fixtures will be much easier to validate than a single broad surface expansion. Gregory’s policy choice is still required before those PRs should start.

207.author: gmkurtzer
207.body: Maintainer review: the implementation is coherent and both required checks are green at current head `e7f5f552747e0b451b6dd31395f9199d10a42ce3`; I found no code-level blocker in the bounded `pollfd` validation or timeout limits. I am not merging it yet because adding `poll` to the balanced surface is an observable policy expansion covered by the unresolved compatibility decision in [issue #179](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/issues/179). Please hold this head while Gregory decides that policy. No revision is requested at this time.

219.author: gmkurtzer
219.body: Maintainer review: the host-information exposure is confirmed by the current balanced surface—`sysinfo` is mediated unchanged in launch/native. This is an observable policy decision, so please continue holding the implementation. The deterministic zero-filled emulation is the safer default than either host passthrough or `-ENOSYS`: it avoids host topology disclosure and avoids glibc deriving values from an uninitialized buffer, without claiming an unenforced domain memory limit. Gregory’s approval is required before opening that PR; `process-native` behavior should remain out of scope for the first change.

222.author: gmkurtzer
222.body:
Thanks for tracing this. I checked the transition history: the removal was **not documented as an intentional overflow-policy decision**. PR #152 made the userspace source at `2306c2e` authoritative; that source already lacked `overflow-checks = true`. The setting existed only in the prior full-kernel lineage from `9b11baea`, so it was not carried across the architecture transition. I found no rationale in PR #152 saying release overflow checks were deliberately disabled or that all arithmetic had become explicitly checked.

The 65/65 result is useful evidence that restoring the setting does not break the unit suite, but the unreviewed `scan_layer` paths, self-start binaries, and release/runtime cost remain open. I am leaving this issue open for the maintainer decision. My recommendation is to restore `overflow-checks = true` as the safer default unless a release benchmark demonstrates a material cost that warrants a documented exception.

PR 224 and 226 are someone else's existing work, not our candidates; track overlap.
